status: completed relevance and independent occurrence-evidence review

review.requirement_proposition: AI actors should respect the rule of law, human rights and democratic and human-centred values throughout the AI lifecycle, including non-discrimination, equality, freedom, dignity, individual autonomy, privacy and data protection, diversity, fairness, social justice and internationally recognised labour rights.
review.reason_for_change: The agentic campaign harvested credentials and domain secrets and exfiltrated credential databases from affected organisations. Its operation failed to respect the privacy and security interests of those affected.

review.requirement_proposition: Document incidents involving third-party GAI data and systems, including open- data and open-source software.
review.reason_for_change: GreyNoise documented the AI-agent architecture, affected systems, credential compromise and targeting deviations. PaperCut separately documented exploitation of the underlying vulnerabilities.

review.requirement_proposition: AI systems should remain robust, secure and safe throughout their entire lifecycle, functioning appropriately without unreasonable safety or security risks under normal use, foreseeable use or misuse and other adverse conditions.
review.reason_for_change: GreyNoise reports AI-orchestrated exploitation of at least 440 instances and credential extraction, including domain-administrator compromise. This is realised security harm under malicious use. The evidence does not isolate the model, harness or orchestration component responsible.

review.requirement_proposition: Design and implement technical controls for agentic components, increased security concerns, and multi-agent interactions to mitigate identified risks.
review.reason_for_change: Hundreds of agents and conventional offensive tools formed the campaign. The sources do not publish the technical controls for their permissions, coordination or targeting. The geographic deviations do not identify one specific failed control.

conclusion_change.previous: AI agents orchestrated a real mass-compromise campaign at a scale and tempo substantially beyond a single assisted intrusion, and the campaign included targets outside an operator-defined geographic exclusion list. The public evidence does not isolate whether those deviations arose from the Codex harness, the DeepSeek model, orchestration logic, target-data state, human configuration or another component. The campaign and its realised cyber harm can therefore be assessed without attributing a model-level failure mechanism or treating malicious use itself as proof of autonomous misbehaviour. Malicious campaign outcomes and DCSync extraction remain distinct from the unresolved target-exclusion control transition and aggregate-role mechanism. The DeepSeek model, Codex harness, operator and conventional tools are not conflated; scale alone supplies no class or external requirement.
conclusion_change.new: The documented campaign caused widespread compromise and credential loss. Those outcomes support privacy and lifecycle-security failures. The campaign was documented, while specific multi-agent controls remain unresolved. The model, harness, operator and conventional tools retain distinct roles.
